flashcard_questions.a: The regulation of the internal conditions of a cell or organism to maintain optimum function.

flashcard_questions.q: Why would a loss of homeostasis stop metabolic reactions?
flashcard_questions.a: Enzymes would denature, so the reactions they catalyse would fail.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the job of a receptor cell in a control system?
flashcard_questions.a: To detect stimuli, which are changes in the environment.

flashcard_questions.q: What is an effector in a control system?
flashcard_questions.a: A muscle or gland that brings about a response.

flashcard_questions.q: Which two organs make up the central nervous system?
Nervous pathway: stimulus, receptor, ____, effector, response.
Reflex arc: receptor, ____ neurone, relay neurone, ____ neurone, effector.
What does a motor neurone do in the nervous pathway?
flashcard_questions.a: It carries electrical impulses from the CNS to effectors.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a synapse between two neurones?
flashcard_questions.a: The tiny gap where a signal crosses chemically from one neurone to the next.

flashcard_questions.q: What chemicals carry a signal across the gap between neurones?
Why can an impulse only travel one way across a synapse?
flashcard_questions.a: Neurotransmitters are released from one side only and bind to receptors on the other.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a reflex action in the body?
flashcard_questions.a: An automatic, rapid response to a stimulus that does not involve the conscious brain.

flashcard_questions.q: What is the typical range of human reaction times?
In the ruler-drop test, what does a greater fall distance show?
In the ruler-drop practical, how should reliability be improved?
flashcard_questions.a: Repeat at least five times and calculate the mean distance.
